summary: Full text confirms that 28661438 tested the complete Lutemax 2020 formulation (24 mg lutein/zeaxanthin/meso-zeaxanthin 83:10:7, one softgel daily for 6 months) in 48 young high-screen-time adults: MPOD, flicker fusion, contrast sensitivity, glare recovery, eye strain and fatigue improved versus placebo, though with no designated primary endpoint and 35:13 allocation. It gets one eligible context for Eye & Vision. The EyePromise trial and the different-ratio inflammation trial are not Lutemax and get no credit. A new applicability block limits credit to eye outcomes.

applicability.studied_population: Healthy young adults (18-25) with at least 6 h/day of screen use taking one 24 mg Lutemax 2020 softgel daily for 6 months (PMID 28661438).

identity.standardization: 24 mg/day total lutein, zeaxanthin and mesozeaxanthin in an 83: 10: 7 ratio, suspended in safflower oil.

population.description: 48 healthy non-smoking students aged 18-25 (mean 21.2; 25 women) with BMI <27 and at least 6 h/day of near-field screen use, University of Georgia; randomized 35 active, 13 placebo.

study_contexts.study_design: 6-month double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial (unequal 35:13 allocation); repeated-measures ANOVA versus placebo at 3 and 6 months; no primary endpoint designated.

dose.administration_frequency: One softgel daily with a meal, preferably lunch or dinner.

normalization.basis: Reported study-material daily dose, not a universal threshold or equivalence to other preparation.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC5532554): Methods 2 and 2.1 (participants, Lutemax 2020 formulation 24 mg L:Z:MZ 83:10:7 in safflower oil, softgel, dosing), statistics, Results paragraph and Table 1, Conflicts of Interest.

co_therapies: Source-reported concurrent-care/restriction context: Subjects were instructed to maintain their current diet;

outcomes.name: Visual performance versus placebo at 6 months: MPOD (p=0.015), critical flicker fusion (p<0.001), contrast sensitivity (p=0.002), disability glare (p=0.021) and photostress recovery (p=0.011) improved.
Symptoms at 6 months: sleep quality (p=0.01), headache frequency (p=0.029), eye strain (p=0.046) and eye fatigue (p=0.016) improved; blurry vision and neck strain did not change.

limitations: Whole mixture, not isolated lutein; multiple outcomes, small trial; exact label ratios required.

The retained full article does not designate a primary outcome/endpoint; recorded hierarchy not_reported. This is a reporting limitation, not invented primary status or completion of any separate approval.
Duration printed as 6 months; duration_days 182 is the 26-week calendar approximation required by the schema, not a source-stated day count.
Small (n=48) trial with 35:13 allocation, many outcomes and no designated primary endpoint; one author consults for the funding sponsor.

This is the complete Lutemax 2020 formulation, matching this branded record; signed A010 rejects attributing the result to isolated lutein. Credit is limited to visual performance and screen-related eye symptoms (Eye & Vision) in young high-screen-time adults.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

identity.standardization: 20 mg Zalone or 26 mg Z+8 mg L+190 mg mixed omega 3

study_contexts.study_design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with separate zeaxanthin-only and zeaxanthin/lutein/omega-3 arms; reported processing-speed analyses pooled the active arms.

dose.administration_frequency: Daily with a meal for four calendar months; the two active formulations remain separate.

normalization.basis: Reported study-material daily dose, not a universal threshold or equivalence to other preparation.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC4176961): Methods intervention paragraph, Results Table 3, Discussion (primary outcome MPOD).

co_therapies: Maintain diet without substantial changes; lutein/zeaxanthin supplementation within preceding six months excluded. Study products taken with meals.

limitations: Not Lutemax preparation; active arms pooled, 28 excluded/lost, omega 3 combination.
34 mg is declared 26+8 carotenoid total, not all formulation mass; no MZ reported.

No credit: EyePromise Zeaxanthin (20 mg zeaxanthin) and vizual EDGE (zeaxanthin, lutein, omega-3) are not the Lutemax 2020 formulation; the reference is already marked scoring_eligible=false. Primary outcome MPOD (Discussion).
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

clinical_review.notes: No credit: the abstract describes L 10 mg + MZ 10 mg + Z 2 mg, not the Lutemax 2020 83:10:7 formulation, and reports inflammatory and oxidized-LDL biomarkers rather than this record's eye or focus goals; full text not retrieved.

limitations: Abstract: 6-month double-blind placebo-controlled trial; versus placebo, IL-1beta (p<0.001), TNF-alpha (p=0.003) and oxLDL fell. Biomarkers only; not cardiovascular event evidence.
